name: Natural Bridge Pipeline
researcher_notes: Not an existing row (no Natural Bridge or Black Hills row in the roster). Qualifies: 35 miles (about 56 km) of new 12-inch steel pipe, above the 25 km rule. Built, so the concrete step is met. The EIA August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 978, lists a completed new intrastate pipeline in Wyoming, in service December 2019, by Black Hills Gas Distribution LLC, 35 miles, 12 inch, cost 54 (millions). The Black Hills Energy project page says a 35-mile, 12-inch steel line from the Casper transmission system to Douglas with regulating stations in Casper and Glenrock, estimated cost 54.2 million dollars, serving 57,000 customers in central Wyoming. The two sources are the operator and a federal statistics release, but EIA likely drew on the operator, so independence is partial. The operator page still says 'building', so the in-service date rests on EIA only. Capacity not stated in either source, left blank. It is a utility supply line, so PipelineType transmission follows the operator's own wording. Owner spelled as EIA gives it, no exact match in the ownership gazetteer. Parent Black Hills Corp is an existing gazetteer entity. Route not found, no official GIS checked beyond the sources above. Intrastate, so FERC silence is not a concern; state regulator filing (Wyoming Public Service Commission) not checked. Start year 2019 would need a ref and is left out.
